## 🌿 Climate & Vegetation → Animal Behavior: A Dynamic Mental Model for Chitwan National Park

### 🔹 1. Climate Overview (Seasonal Cycles)

Chitwan has a **humid subtropical monsoon climate (Cwa)** with distinct seasonal shifts:

| Season | Climate Features |
|-------|------------------|
| **Monsoon (Mid-June to Late September)** | High humidity, heavy rainfall (up to 2,500 mm/year), dense cloud cover, frequent flooding, high temperatures (up to 36°C) |
| **Post-Monsoon / Dry Season (Mid-October to Late December)** | Monsoon retreats, humidity drops, temperatures fall gradually from ~36°C to 18°C (daytime), nights cool to 5°C, occasional light rains in December |
| **Winter (Late December to February)** | Gradual warming, dry conditions, low humidity, clear skies, cold nights |

> 📌 *Key transition point:* The **end of the monsoon** (mid-October) marks a shift from wet to dry conditions — this triggers ecological changes in vegetation and animal movement.

---

### 🔹 2. Vegetation Zones & Seasonal Dynamics

| Vegetation Type | Location | Seasonal Behavior |
|----------------|--------|-------------------|
| **Himalayan subtropical broadleaf forests (Sal trees)** | Central lowlands, well-drained ground | Dominant in dry season; dense canopy provides shelter. Sal trees grow best in well-drained soils. |
| **Chir Pine (Pinus roxburghii)** | Southern face of Churia Hills | More common in drier, exposed slopes; grows during dry season. |
| **Riverine forests & grasslands** | Along Narayani-Rapti river system | Flooded during monsoon, dry and exposed in post-monsoon. |
| **Terai-Duar savanna & grasslands (20% of park)** | Lowland floodplains | Colonized by grasses like *Saccharum ravennae*, *Arundo donax*, *Phragmites karka*; flooded during monsoon, dry and lush in post-monsoon. |
| **Alluvial floodplains** | Riverbanks, oxbow lakes | Seasonally flooded; grasslands emerge after floods. |

> 📌 *Key transition:* After monsoon floods, **new grasses colonize sandbanks**, and **lush grasslands emerge** — this is a critical trigger for herbivores.

---

### 🔹 3. Animal Behavior Linked to Climate & Vegetation

Now, we link each animal group to **specific behavioral responses** based on climate and vegetation changes.

---

#### 🐘 **Indian Rhinoceros (Sariska, Greater One-Horned)**

- **Climate link:** Monsoon floods → riverine forests and grasslands are submerged.
- **Vegetation link:** Rhinos prefer **rhino apple trees (Trewia nudiflora)** and **rosewood (Dalbergia sissoo)** — both found in riverine zones and dry grasslands.
- **Behavioral response:**
  - **Monsoon (wet):** Rhinos are confined to higher, drier forested areas or riverine forests where trees are present.
  - **Post-monsoon (dry):** As grasslands emerge and vegetation dries, rhinos move into **open grasslands** to browse on grasses and fruits.
  - **Seasonal movement:** They are **most active in dry season** when food is accessible.
  - **Conservation note:** Poaching peaks during dry season when animals are more visible and movement is predictable.

> ✅ *Behavioral insight:* Rhinos are **seasonally mobile**, shifting from forested hills to grasslands as the monsoon ends and grasses grow.

---

- **Vegetation link:** Tigers rely on **alluvial floodplains** and **dense forests** for hunting and denning.
